name: DeepDiff
baseline: Other Swift diffing libraries (Differ, Dwifft, Changeset, ListDiff); the standard library's difference(from:) did not exist yet
verdict_reason: The ranking holds: in DifferenceKit's later release-build run DeepDiff still beats the Myers-based libraries and the standard library. The size of the gap does not: the README's Dwifft and Changeset timings of 77-150 seconds come from single Date()-timed runs in a project with no shared scheme, which most likely means a debug build, and in a release build Dwifft took 0.47 s on a larger input. DeepDiff also only tied IGListKit and ran about 20x slower than DifferenceKit.
tier_reason: First-party, single-shot timings on an iPhone 6 with no build configuration stated; benchmark code is public.
claimed_speedup: 2000 to 2100 UUID strings (100 deletions, 200 insertions): DeepDiff 0.0451 s, Differ 0.2 s, ListDiff 0.106 s, Changeset 77.6 s, Dwifft 150 s. Independent release-build check (DifferenceKit, 5,000 UUIDs): DeepDiff 0.0373 s vs 0.0620 s for Swift.CollectionDifference. Times rounded to three significant figures from the raw results.
workload: Arrays of 36-character UUID strings; 2,000 old items, new array with 100 deletions and 200 insertions; one timed call per library.
toolchain: Not stated (Swift 4-5 era; benchmark project has no shared scheme, so Xcode's default Run uses the Debug configuration)
one_liner: Heckel-based Swift diff for table and collection views; faster than Myers libraries, but its own benchmark overstates the gap.
how_it_is_fast: DeepDiff uses Heckel's linear-time algorithm with a hashable diffId per element, plus a move reducer adapted from HeckelDiff. Earlier versions used Wagner-Fischer, which is O(mn) and only suitable for small lists.
use_it_when: Existing code already depends on it and lists are moderate in size
skip_it_when: New code: the repository is archived, and DifferenceKit measured about 20x faster in the same release build
caveats: Each library was timed once with Date() inside viewWillAppear, with no warm-up or repetition.

The Benchmark project ships no shared scheme, so a default Run uses Debug (-Onone) for the app and its CocoaPods; Dwifft's 149.6 s here versus 0.4732 s for a larger input in DifferenceKit's -O run points to an unoptimized build.
iPhone 6 in early 2018 with library versions of that time (Dwifft 0.8, Differ 1.0.3, Changeset 3.0, ListDiff 0.1.0).
GitHub reports the license as NOASSERTION; LICENSE.md contains MIT text.
tradeoffs: Elements must conform to DiffAware (diffId plus content comparison)
Archived: no fixes for newer Swift versions
